items.stem: Which term is defined as "a process involving the fusion of the nuclei of two gametes to form a zygote and the production of offspring that are genetically different from each other"?
items.answer: Sexual reproduction
items.markingKey: Sexual reproduction: a process involving the fusion of the nuclei of two gametes to form a zygote and the production of offspring that are genetically different from each other.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "asexual reproduction"?
options: A sex cell, such as a sperm, egg, pollen nucleus or ovule nucleus, with a haploid nucleus.
The diploid cell formed when two gametes fuse at fertilisation.
A process resulting in the production of genetically identical offspring from one parent.
A process involving the fusion of the nuclei of two gametes to form a zygote and the production of offspring that are genetically different from each other.
items.answer: A process resulting in the production of genetically identical offspring from one parent.
items.markingKey: Asexual reproduction: a process resulting in the production of genetically identical offspring from one parent.

items.stem: Explain why farmers often grow crops such as bananas from cuttings rather than seeds.
items.answer: Cuttings produce clones with the same desirable characteristics (e.g. yield, taste); it is quick and reliable.

items.stem: Which type of reproduction is shown by bacteria dividing by binary fission?
items.answer: asexual
items.markingKey: Bacteria dividing by binary fission: asexual reproduction.

items.stem: In a region near Kathmandu, most farmers grow the same variety of banana, propagated asexually from cuttings. A new fungal disease has started to spread. (a) Explain why the new disease is a serious threat. (b) Suggest how scientists could use sexual reproduction to help.
items.answer: (a) All plants are genetically identical so none has resistance; disease can spread through the whole crop. (b) Cross-breed varieties to produce varied offspring and select those resistant to the disease.

items.stem: Which is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
options: Only one parent is needed and it is fast
It helps species adapt to change
items.answer: Only one parent is needed and it is fast
items.markingKey: No need to find a mate or pollinator; many offspring quickly.

items.stem: Explain why a field of genetically identical plants is at risk from a new disease.
items.answer: If one plant is susceptible, all are, since there is no genetic variation; the disease could destroy the whole crop.

items.stem: Which type of reproduction is shown by a potato tuber growing new shoots?
items.answer: asexual
items.markingKey: A potato tuber growing new shoots: asexual reproduction.

items.stem: A bean plant producing seeds in pods. (a) State the type of reproduction. (b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of this type of reproduction for the plant.
items.answer: (a) sexual (b) advantage: variation, adaptation to change, seed dispersal; disadvantage: needs pollinators / slower / more energy.
items.markingKey: (a) sexual [1] (b) advantage [1]; disadvantage [1] [3]

items.stem: Bees carrying pollen between apple flowers and seeds forming. (a) State the type of reproduction. (b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of this type of reproduction for the plant.
items.answer: (a) sexual (b) advantage: variation, adaptation to change, seed dispersal; disadvantage: needs pollinators / slower / more energy.
items.markingKey: (a) sexual [1] (b) advantage [1]; disadvantage [1] [3]

items.stem: In a region near Dubai, most farmers grow the same variety of banana, propagated asexually from cuttings. A new fungal disease has started to spread. (a) Explain why asexual propagation is popular with farmers. (b) Suggest how scientists could use sexual reproduction to help.
items.answer: (a) Quick; offspring identical, so they keep high yield and quality; no pollination needed. (b) Cross-breed varieties to produce varied offspring and select those resistant to the disease.

items.stem: In a region near Lima, most farmers grow the same variety of potato, propagated asexually from cuttings. A new fungal disease has started to spread. (a) Explain why the new disease is a serious threat. (b) Evaluate the use of asexual reproduction for this crop.
items.answer: (a) All plants are genetically identical so none has resistance; disease can spread through the whole crop. (b) Advantages: uniform, fast, reliable. Disadvantages: no variation, vulnerable to disease and climate change. Best to keep a variety of strains / use sexual breeding to introduce resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) advantage [1]; disadvantage [1]; conclusion [1] [3]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "pollination"?
options: The transfer of pollen from an anther of a flower to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species.
The transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma.
The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma of the same flower or another flower on the same plant.
items.answer: The transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma.
items.markingKey: Pollination: the transfer of pollen grains from an anther to a stigma.

items.stem: Explain how the structure of an insect-pollinated flower is adapted to pollination.
items.answer: Bright petals and scent attract insects; nectar is a reward; anthers and sticky stigma positioned so the insect brushes against them; sticky/spiky pollen sticks to insects.
items.markingKey: attraction [1]; positions of anther/stigma [1]; pollen type [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why grasses do not have brightly coloured petals.
items.answer: They are wind-pollinated, so they do not need to attract insects; energy is saved.

items.stem: A flower has scent and nectar, large, brightly coloured petals, stigma inside the flower, sticky. How is it pollinated?
items.answer: by insects
items.markingKey: large, brightly coloured petals; scent and nectar; anthers inside the flower; stigma inside the flower, sticky; small amounts of large, sticky or spiky pollen → insect-pollinated.

items.stem: A plant found near Toronto has flowers with anthers inside the flower, scent and nectar, stigma inside the flower, sticky. (a) Suggest how the flower is pollinated. (b) Explain how two of these features help pollination. (c) Describe how the anthers would differ in a flower pollinated by wind.
items.answer: (a) insect pollination (b) features attract insects / pollen sticks to insect (c) anthers hanging outside the flower on long filaments
items.markingKey: (a) insect [1] (b) two features explained [2] (c) anthers hanging outside the flower on long filaments [1] [4]

items.stem: A student compares flowers of grass (wind-pollinated) and hibiscus (insect-pollinated). (a) Describe two features you would expect to see in the grass flower. (b) Distinguish between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
items.answer: (a) small, dull or no petals; no scent or nectar. (b) Self: pollen to stigma of same flower / same plant. Cross: pollen to stigma of a different plant of the same species.

items.stem: Which feature is typical of a wind-pollinated flower?
items.answer: Feathery stigmas outside the flower
items.markingKey: Feathery stigmas catch pollen from the air.

items.stem: Explain why self-pollination may be a disadvantage to a species.
items.answer: Less genetic variation, so the population is less able to adapt to changes such as new diseases.

items.stem: A student in Bogotá states: "Pollination is the same as fertilisation." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen; fertilisation is the fusion of the pollen nucleus with the ovule nucleus.

items.stem: State the function of each part of a flower: (i) ovary, (ii) style, (iii) anther.
items.answer: (i) contains ovules and develops into the fruit (ii) connects the stigma to the ovary; the pollen tube grows down it (iii) produces pollen

items.stem: Compare the structure of insect-pollinated and wind-pollinated flowers, explaining how each is adapted to its method of pollination.
items.answer: Insect: large bright petals, scent, nectar, anthers/stigma inside, sticky stigma, small amount of sticky/spiky pollen. Wind: small/no petals, no scent/nectar, anthers hang outside, feathery stigma outside, large amounts of light smooth pollen.

items.stem: A student compares flowers of grass (wind-pollinated) and orchid (insect-pollinated). (a) Describe two features you would expect to see in the grass flower. (b) Explain how the stigma of the orchid flower is adapted. (c) Distinguish between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
items.answer: (a) small, dull or no petals; no scent or nectar. (b) stigma inside the flower, sticky— pollen sticks to it when insects brush past. (c) Self: pollen to stigma of same flower / same plant. Cross: pollen to stigma of a different plant of the same species.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "germination"?
options: A structure that develops from a fertilised ovule, containing an embryo and a food store.
A tube that grows from a pollen grain down the style to carry the male nucleus to the ovule.
A structure that develops from the ovary after fertilisation and contains seeds.
The start of growth of a seed into a seedling.
items.answer: The start of growth of a seed into a seedling.
items.markingKey: Germination: the start of growth of a seed into a seedling.

items.stem: Explain why seeds do not germinate in very cold soil.
items.answer: Enzymes that break down food stores and control respiration work very slowly at low temperature.

items.stem: Explain why seeds sown in waterlogged soil may not germinate.
items.answer: Water fills the air spaces, so there is too little oxygen for aerobic respiration.

items.stem: Sipho placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 5, 10, 16, 19, 18, 13; trial 2: 5, 10, 15, 19, 17, 12; trial 3: 5, 10, 16, 19, 18, 13. Calculate the mean number of seeds germinated at 10 °C.

Arjun placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 2, 9, 18, 14, 4; trial 2: 2, 9, 19, 14, 4; trial 3: 2, 5, 18, 14, 4. items.stem: Explain why a seed needs a food store.
items.answer: The embryo cannot photosynthesise until leaves are above ground; the food store provides energy (by respiration) and materials for growth.

items.stem: A flower has stigma inside the flower, sticky, scent and nectar, anthers inside the flower. How is it pollinated?
items.answer: by insects
items.markingKey: large, brightly coloured petals; scent and nectar; anthers inside the flower; stigma inside the flower, sticky; small amounts of large, sticky or spiky pollen → insect-pollinated.

items.stem: Scientists counted pollen grains produced per anther: an insect-pollinated flower produced 639 and a wind-pollinated grass produced 59 100. Calculate how many times more pollen the grass produced, and explain the difference.
items.answer: 92 times; wind pollination is random, so most pollen never reaches a stigma; insects carry pollen directly between flowers.
items.markingKey: 59 100 ÷ 639 = 92 [1]; random dispersal / most lost [1]; insects more targeted [1] [3]

items.stem: State the function of each part of a flower: (i) stigma, (ii) sepal, (iii) ovule.
items.answer: (i) receives pollen during pollination (ii) protects the flower bud (iii) contains the female gamete and develops into the seed

items.stem: A student compares flowers of mango (insect-pollinated) and rice (wind-pollinated). (a) Describe two features you would expect to see in the mango flower. (b) Explain how the stigma of the rice flower is adapted.
items.answer: (a) large, brightly coloured petals; scent and nectar. (b) large feathery stigmas outside the flower— catches pollen from the air.

items.stem: A student compares flowers of grass (wind-pollinated) and mango (insect-pollinated). (a) Describe two features you would expect to see in the grass flower. (b) Explain how the stigma of the mango flower is adapted. (c) Distinguish between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
items.answer: (a) small, dull or no petals; no scent or nectar. (b) stigma inside the flower, sticky— pollen sticks to it when insects brush past. (c) Self: pollen to stigma of same flower / same plant. Cross: pollen to stigma of a different plant of the same species.

items.stem: Describe how a pollen nucleus reaches the ovule.
items.answer: A pollen tube grows from the pollen grain down through the style into the ovary and through the micropyle into the ovule.

items.stem: Leila says: "The fruit develops from the petals." Explain whether Leila is correct.
items.answer: The fruit develops from the ovary wall.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: The fruit develops from the ovary wall. [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why seeds sown in waterlogged soil may not germinate. (b) Explain why seeds do not germinate in very cold soil.
items.answer: (a) Water fills the air spaces, so there is too little oxygen for aerobic respiration. (b) Enzymes that break down food stores and control respiration work very slowly at low temperature.

items.stem: Kwame placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 2, 5, 10, 16, 19, 17; trial 2: 2, 5, 10, 16, 18, 18; trial 3: 2, 5, 10, 16, 19, 17. State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: Number and type of seeds; volume of water.
items.markingKey: Any two from: number and type of seeds; volume of water; light conditions; time allowed [2]

items.stem: Hana placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 8, 13, 18, 19, 15, 10; trial 2: 8, 19, 17, 19, 15, 9; trial 3: 8, 13, 18, 18, 16, 10. Calculate the mean number of seeds germinated at 15 °C, ignoring any anomalous result.

Jonas placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 3, 6, 11, 16, 20, 17; trial 2: 3, 6, 11, 17, 26, 16; trial 3: 3, 6, 12, 17, 18, 17. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (c) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis. (d) Calculate the mean percentage germination at the temperature with the highest mean number of seeds germinated.
items.answer: (a) Independent: temperature; dependent: number of seeds germinated. (b) Number and type of seeds; volume of water. (c) A line graph: temperature on the x-axis and mean number of seeds germinated on the y-axis. (d) 95%
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = temperature [1]; dependent variable = number of seeds germinated [1] [2] (b) Any two from: number and type of seeds; volume of water; light conditions; time allowed [2] (c) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; temperature on x-axis and number of seeds germinated on y-axis [1] [2] (d) 19 ÷ 20 [1] × 100 = 95% [1] [2]

items.stem: Mei placed 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool in each of several dishes at different temperatures and counted the number that germinated after 5 days. Results table. Temperature / °C: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. Number of seeds germinated, trial 1: 2, 10, 19, 14, 4; trial 2: 2, 10, 19, 13, 3; trial 3: 3, 9, 19, 13, 4. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. (c) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) Independent: temperature; dependent: number of seeds germinated. (b) Use more seeds in each dish. (c) A line graph: temperature on the x-axis and mean number of seeds germinated on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = temperature [1]; dependent variable = number of seeds germinated [1] [2] (b) Any one from: use more seeds in each dish; keep each dish in an incubator at the exact temperature; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the temperature (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1] (c) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; temperature on x-axis and number of seeds germinated on y-axis [1] [2]
